I farm the way I have seen work here in Quzhou for many years. I do not start from zero every year. I look at what I planted last year, how the water was, and what gave a steady harvest. My land is 10.1 mu, not too small and not too big, so I can still count costs carefully, but I will spend if it protects yield. Wheat and maize are my main food-and-cash fields, and with well water I will not let them dry at the key time. For wheat, I will keep fertilizer a bit stronger because weak wheat in spring is hard to fix later. For maize, I will also feed it enough, because if the ear is small, the loss is real. Cotton takes more watching and more pesticide, but if I manage it well it still brings cash, so I will keep a smaller piece in cotton instead of putting all land into wheat-maize. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen neighbors get better stands and better yield, but I will not go too fancy. I will plough or rotary till the land clean, put on enough base fertilizer, irrigate at the important stages, and spray when insects and disease start showing instead of waiting too long.
